questions.q: In a Redshift cluster, which node stores table data?
options: Neither — Redshift always reads from S3 at query time
The leader node only
Both store an identical full copy of every table
Compute nodes — the leader node stores no table data
questions.explain: The leader node coordinates query planning and result assembly; compute nodes store table data and do the actual scanning and processing.

questions.q: What does the leader node do when it receives a SQL query?
options: Parses and optimizes it, splits it into steps compute nodes run in parallel, and assembles the final result
Executes the entire query itself, then discards the compute nodes' work
Nothing — compute nodes receive queries directly from the client
Forwards the raw SQL unchanged to S3
questions.explain: You always connect to the leader node's endpoint; it plans and coordinates, while compute nodes execute the actual work.

questions.q: Why does columnar storage make an aggregation query like SUM(amount) faster on a wide table?
options: It automatically deletes unused columns from disk
It converts all queries into row-by-row scans
It stores every row twice for redundancy
It reads only the columns the query actually touches, instead of every column in every row
questions.explain: Columnar storage groups each column's values together on disk, so a query only pays the I/O cost of the columns it references.

options: A subdivision of a compute node's memory and disk, and the real unit of parallel query execution
A backup copy of the leader node
A synonym for an entire compute node
A billing unit used only by Redshift Serverless
questions.explain: Each compute node is divided into slices, each with its own share of memory and disk; more slices means more concurrent pieces of a query can run.

questions.q: What does MPP (massively parallel processing) mean in the context of Redshift?
options: It's a synonym for columnar storage
Redshift processes one row at a time across the whole cluster
Multiple unrelated queries are merged into a single query
One query is split into pieces that run concurrently across compute nodes and their slices
questions.explain: MPP is the parallel execution model: the leader node distributes a query's work across all compute nodes and slices to run simultaneously.
